issues.description: PR title/description and code/CHANGELOG disagree on the check name and semantics
issues.detail: The PR title says 'compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces' and describes PASS/FAIL only. The code, metadata, tests, and CHANGELOG actually ship 'compute_instance_single_network_interface' with a third state (MANUAL for gke- prefix). This is THREE-PATCHES masquerading as one: (1) add network_interfaces to the model, (2) add the basic check, (3) add GKE auto-classification. The GKE heuristic in particular is undocumented in the PR body and adds a special case on a string prefix that any user can name a non-GKE VM with. Pick a name, pick a behavior, and make the PR description match what the code does. Right now nobody reviewing this knows what they're approving.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is a bad-taste special case
issues.detail: Classifying an instance as GKE-managed because its name starts with 'gke-' is exactly the kind of special case good taste eliminates. Any user can name a VM 'gke-foo' and silently downgrade a FAIL to MANUAL; conversely, GKE node names can be customized in some configurations. The correct signal lives in instance labels (goog-gke-node, goog-k8s-node-name) or in the managed-instance-group / metadata. If you want to exempt GKE, read the actual GKE-managed signal from the API, not from a substring of a user-controlled string. If you can't get the real signal in this patch, drop the MANUAL branch entirely and let the user suppress findings the normal way.

issues.description: Dead-code branch for zero network interfaces reports PASS
issues.detail: The else branch (interface_count == 0) leaves report.status as 'PASS' and writes 'has no network interfaces.' A VM with zero NICs is not a passing single-NIC instance; it's either an API edge case or a state worth flagging separately. Either drop the branch (GCE instances always have at least one NIC and the API guarantees it) or set an explicit status. Don't silently pass on impossible data.

issues.description: Diff conflates a model change with a check and isn't reviewed as such
issues.detail: The compute_service.py change adds a NetworkInterface model and populates it inside _get_instances. That belongs in its own patch with its own test coverage (the service_test only checks len()). Bundling it with a new check means the model change gets reviewed by check reviewers and the check gets reviewed by service reviewers, and both get it wrong. Split: patch 1 adds NetworkInterface + populates the field + tests the field. Patch 2 adds the check on top.

issues.description: Stripping the URL prefix off network/subnetwork loses information
issues.detail: interface.get('network', '').split('/')[-1] throws away the project and region context that GCP returns in the self-link. If two interfaces are on a 'default' network in different projects, you can't tell them apart in the model. Store the full self-link and derive the short name when displaying. Cheap to do right now, expensive to fix later when another check needs the project.

issues.description: CHANGELOG entry is in the wrong section ordering and uses one name while the PR title uses another
issues.detail: Minor, but the CHANGELOG line refers to compute_instance_single_network_interface (matching the code) while the PR is titled compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces. Pick one. Whoever cherry-picks this for backport will read the title.

issues.description: interface_names computed unconditionally even when only count is needed
issues.detail: interface_names is built for every instance even though it's only used in the PASS-with-one and the multi-NIC branches. Trivial cost, but the more interesting smell is that the same f-string pattern is rebuilt three times. The function is small enough that it's fine, but a maintainer six years from now will appreciate one status_extended assembly site instead of three near-identical ones.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch ships a real check but its name, behavior, and PR description don't agree, and it smuggles in a GKE auto-exemption that nobody asked the reviewer to evaluate. The 'gke-' prefix sniff is BAD-TASTE: a special case on a user-controllable string standing in for a real signal that GCP actually exposes (labels, managed-instance-group membership). This is THREE-PATCHES presented as one: NetworkInterface model + basic single-NIC check + GKE heuristic. Split it. Fix the name mismatch, kill the prefix check or replace it with the real GKE signal, decide what zero-NIC means, and resubmit.
